nyc_found: By law, there are 13,587 yellow taxis in New York City, and each must have a medallion attached to its hood.
match_found: Taxi vehicle licences - 13,483 a decrease of 28 on the previous week, there were 2 new licences issued (week ending 16 August 2026)
finding: Both numbers verify exactly. The NYC figure is a fixed legal cap set by law while the TfL figure is a live weekly licence count that moves week to week, but the caveat already tells readers both sides are licence counts and that about a fifth of NYC medallions sit idle, so the mismatch is disclosed rather than hidden.

nyc_found: The Ferry carries over 16 million passengers annually on a 5.2-mile run between the St. George Terminal in Staten Island and the Whitehall Terminal in Lower Manhattan.
match_found: Patronage: 15.5m annually (Transdev Sydney Ferries fast facts)
conflict: Wikipedia's Sydney Ferries patronage chart, sourced from official reporting (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Ferries), lists financial-year 2024-25 patronage at 19.1 million -- above both the 15.5 million used in the claim and the Staten Island Ferry's own current figure (16,692,900 for 2025, per the same Wikipedia page). If the newer count is used, Sydney's ferries carry more riders than Staten Island's, not roughly the same.
finding: The claim says 'all of Sydney's' ferry passengers, but the 15.5 million figure comes from a Transdev press release dated 20 May 2024 that covers only Transdev's own contracted network. Sydney has other ferry operators not included in that count, including Manly Fast Ferry (NRMA-owned) and tourist operators like Captain Cook Cruises. The source is also more than two years old, and the best available newer figure (19.1 million, FY2024-25) is meaningfully higher and would reverse which city's ferry system carries more. No caveat discloses any of this.

nyc_found: The Metropolitan Museum of Art welcomed over 5.7 million visitors to its two locations—The Met Fifth Avenue and The Met Cloisters—in the fiscal year that ended on June 30, 2025
match_found: the Uffizi with 5.3 million over its three interconnected sites in Florence
conflict: The Art Newspaper article used as the Uffizi source (https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2026/03/31/exclusive-the-worlds-100-most-visited-museums-in-2025-new-museums-a-big-hit-with-visitors) also reports the Met's calendar-year 2025 attendance as 'almost 6 million visitors to its main building,' with a combined total of 6,265,898 including the Cloisters -- both higher than the 5.7 million fiscal-year figure the claim uses.
finding: Both headline numbers verify and the caveat correctly discloses that each museum's total spans multiple sites (Met Fifth Avenue plus the Cloisters; the Uffizi gallery, Pitti Palace and Boboli Gardens). But the same publication cited for the Uffizi number shows a noticeably higher, more recent Met figure, because the Met's fiscal year (ending June) and the Uffizi's calendar year cover different 12-month windows -- a reader comparing them side by side would land on a different gap.

finding: Both figures are from the same Broadway League 2024-2025 season and verify exactly. As of early September 2026 the League has not yet published a 2025-2026 season wrap, so this is the most current data available.

nyc_found: Across the city, murder declined by 20.2% (305 vs. 382), with 77 fewer murders compared to 2024.
match_found: the number of homicides reported to the Houston Police Department declined from 331 to 272
conflict: NYPD's own Fiscal 2025 Mayor's Management Report (https://www.nyc.gov/assets/operations/downloads/pdf/mmr2025/nypd.pdf) lists 'Murder and non-negligent manslaughter' for FY25 (July 2024-June 2025) at 339, not 305 -- a different official NYPD count because it runs on a fiscal year rather than calendar 2025.
finding: Both cited figures verify for calendar year 2025, and the caveat correctly warns that Houston's much smaller population means its murder rate is about three times New York's. Worth noting for the record: NYPD's own fiscal-year report shows a different murder total (339) for an overlapping but non-identical 12-month period, so the 'right' NYPD murder number depends on which official NYPD document you open.
